propositions: Plan review and code review currently discover policies through partially independent registries and routing paths, allowing one gate to disable built-ins, omit project criteria, ignore applicability rules, or misclassify failed work as successful checkpoints.

The new unified architecture must derive selection from one immutable effective-policy snapshot shared between both review gates, with gate-owned strategies for context/topology and a shared executor for typed outcomes, budget enforcement, and checkpoint mechanics.

Project code-review LLM criteria must require non-empty repository-relative globs with `["**"]` representing repository-wide scope; `project.review-phase-boundaries` must migrate from empty-list to explicit repository-wide convention without changing membership.

The `rebar review-plan --retry` command must reuse content-identical successful outcomes, retry only missing calls with a fresh attempt budget, and refuse stale or unreadable lineages before any model call.

Plan review must preserve chunking, concurrency, caching, and checkpointing behavior while moving to digest-complete success-only checkpoint namespaces that are incompatible with legacy checkpoint envelopes.
The workflow editor must separate editable Authored Workflow from read-only Effective Policy and reject empty project code-review LLM glob lists with `["**"]` as the remedy.
